specialSystems.description: Beyond standard weapons and shields, SFB ships have special systems that provide unique tactical capabilities.

systems.name: Cloaking Device
systems.description: Makes a ship invisible or 'fuzzy' to enemy sensors. Primarily used by Romulans.
systems.energyCost: Varies by ship. Requires energy allocation each turn.
rules: A cloaked ship cannot fire weapons or use most active systems while cloaked.
Cloaked ships can be detected by the 'flash cube' effect — detonating an explosive (mine or T-bomb) near them reveals their position.
Default cloaking rules make the ship 'fuzzy' — opponents know approximately where it is but not precisely enough to target effectively.
Optional rules allow complete invisibility under some circumstances.
Ships cannot use EM (Electronic Measures) while cloaked.
tacticalNotes: Cloaking enables ambush tactics and surprise attacks.
Decloaking takes time — plan when and where to reveal yourself.
Enemy ECM can sometimes detect cloaked ships.

systems.name: Tractor Beams
systems.description: Used to retrieve small objects and tow starships. Standard equipment on most starships.
rules: May be used at any speed.
May be activated during any impulse. Once attached, can be released during any impulse.
Each tractor beam may only be used once per turn. Once released, cannot be reused for 8 impulses.
No firing arcs — can be used in any direction.
Used to tow starships, hold seeking weapons (drones), and prevent enemy maneuvers.
uses: Holding enemy drones to prevent them from reaching their target
Gorn Anchor — preventing victims from launching wild weasel decoys
Tractor-repulsor beams (Andromedan) — used as weapons to shake targets apart
limitations: Shuttles are destroyed if towed at high speed.
Plasma torpedoes cannot be held by tractor beams (only drones).

systems.name: Transporters
systems.description: Beam personnel, objects, or bombs between ships or to planets.
rules: Transporters will not function through shields. A ship may need to drop a shield to use transporters.
Work on a direct line from ship to ship.
To determine which shield must be dropped, use the same rules as for direct-fire weapons.
A dropped shield must remain down for 1/4 turn (8 impulses).
Cannot transport through objects (including shuttle pilots, cloaking devices) without permission due to security systems.
uses: Boarding parties — beam marines onto enemy ships with downed shields
Transporter Bombs (T-Bombs) — beam explosives onto enemy ships or into their path
tacticalNotes: Boarding parties transported from another fleet are considered hostile.
T-Bombs are a favorite Andromedan tactic.
Dropping shields for transporters creates vulnerability.

systems.name: Electronic Warfare (EW)
systems.description: ECM (Electronic Countermeasures) and ECCM (Electronic Counter-Countermeasures) affect weapons fire and sensor effectiveness.
rules: ECM reduces incoming damage from enemy weapons fire.
ECCM maintains own weapons effectiveness against enemy ECM.
At medium to long ranges, ECM can be more efficient than shield reinforcement.
Cannot fire seeking weapons while using EM (Electronic Measures).
EW may not be lent between fleets.
tacticalNotes: With max ECM and EM, you should rarely take damage at medium range.
EW is a key defensive tool, especially for ships with weaker shields.
Electronic warfare range limitations may be waived in small engagements (no more than 2 ships per side, 5 total).

systems.name: Labs
systems.description: Scientific laboratories used to scan and analyze unknown objects, space monsters, or enemy weapons.
rules: Labs are used to identify unknown ships, space monsters, or weapon types.
Effectiveness depends on closest approach and lab rating.
In Federation Commander (simplified version), no die roll — automatic number of points based on closest approach.
uses: Identifying space monsters and their vulnerabilities

systems.name: Sensors
systems.description: Detect and track enemy ships. Determine what information is visible to the player. Functionally similar to 20th century radar but operating on different principles for FTL targets.
rules: Sensor rating determines detection range and accuracy.
Can see the SSD of an opponent's ship at a range of 5x the number of sensors.
Sensor lock-on is required for some weapons fire.
Sensors can detect cloaked ships under certain conditions (especially with ECM).
Sensors and scanners broadcast an electronic pulse reflected back by targets.
Computers analyze returns to gain information about the target.
Certain known targets (asteroids, Klingon frigates, plasma torpedoes) have specific sensor signatures.
The last sensor box is always 0 — represents residual capability after effective destruction.

detectionRanges.description: Sensor rating affects what can be detected and at what range.
detectionRanges.ssdDetection: Can see opponent's SSD at range of 5x sensor rating.
detectionRanges.cloakedDetection: ECM can sometimes detect cloaked ships.

systems.name: Scanners
systems.description: Provide additional information about enemy ships and terrain. Work in conjunction with sensors.
rules: Scanner rating determines the level of detail available about enemy ships.
Can reveal ship class, damage status, and other information at close range.
The last scanner box is always 9 — represents residual capability after effective destruction.
Scanners help identify unknown ships and space monsters.

scannerRatings.description: Lower scanner numbers = better scanning capability.

systems.name: Batteries
systems.description: Store energy from previous turns for use as Reserve Power.
rules: Limited capacity — varies by ship.
Reserve Power allows activating systems not allocated in the Energy Allocation phase.
Useful for emergency situations — powering up shields or weapons mid-turn.

systems.name: Capacitors
systems.description: Store energy specifically for weapon overload.
rules: Allow weapons to fire at increased damage without allocating overload energy in the Energy Allocation phase.
Limited capacity — varies by ship.

systems.name: Wild Weasels
systems.description: Decoy shuttlecraft launched to fool enemy seeking weapons into locking onto the wrong target.
rules: Shuttles are launched and programmed to attract seeking weapon fire.
Effective against plasma torpedoes and drones.
Suicide shuttles can be charged with anti-matter bombs and fired unmanned as seeking weapons.

systems.name: Fire Control Systems
systems.description: Sensors, scanners, and electronic warfare systems that control weapons targeting.

disruptedFireControl.description: When fire control is disrupted (e.g., by EW or damage), weapons effectiveness is reduced.
